body_html:
Multiply by 10, 100 and 1000

When you multiply a whole number by 10, 100 or 1000, every digit moves to the left. When you divide, every digit moves to the right.

CalculationEvery digit movesZeros
× 10 or ÷ 101 placewrite or take away 1 zero
× 100 or ÷ 1002 placeswrite or take away 2 zeros
× 1000 or ÷ 10003 placeswrite or take away 3 zeros

Divide by 10, 100 and 1000

Example

5 200 000 ÷ 1000

Every digit moves 3 places to the right. Take away the last 3 zeros.

Answer: 5200

Multiples of 10, 100 and 1000

Split the multiple into a basic fact and a power of 10: 30 = 3 × 10 and 400 = 4 × 100.

Example

500 × 800

5 × 8 = 40. Then write 2 + 2 = 4 more zeros.

Answer: 400 000

Estimate first

Round each number, then use the rules above. 38 × 52 ≈ 40 × 50 = 2000. An estimate shows if an answer is reasonable.

Word problems: draw a model

Example

1200 pupils are put into classes of 40. How many classes are there?

1200 ÷ 40: 1200 ÷ 10 = 120, and 120 ÷ 4 = 30.

Answer: 30 classes

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
2500 × 100 = 25 000 (1 zero written)× 100 writes 2 zeros: 250 000
70 500 ÷ 100 = 75 (the wrong zero taken away)Take away the last zeros only: 705
400 × 30 = 1200Count all the zeros: 2 + 1 = 3, so 12 000
500 × 800 = 40 0005 × 8 = 40 has its own zero: 400 000
2400 ÷ 20 = 24 (÷ 10, then ÷ 10 again)20 = 10 × 2: ÷ 10, then ÷ 2, so 120

faq.q: How do you multiply and divide by 10, 100 and 1000 in P5?
faq.a: Move every digit 1, 2 or 3 places: to the left to multiply and to the right to divide. For whole numbers, write or take away the same number of zeros at the end, so 406 × 100 = 40 600 and 70 500 ÷ 100 = 705.

faq.q: How do I explain 400 × 30 to my child?
faq.a: Split each number into a basic fact and a power of 10: 400 × 30 = 4 × 3 × 1000. Work out 4 × 3 = 12, then write 3 zeros to get 12 000.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake?
faq.a: Writing or taking away the wrong number of zeros, such as 400 × 30 = 1200 or 2400 ÷ 20 = 24. Count the zeros in both numbers, and remember that 20 is 10 × 2, not 10 × 10.

faq.q: Is this in the MOE syllabus?
faq.a: Yes. Multiplying and dividing by 10, 100, 1000 and their multiples without a calculator is part of Whole Numbers in the MOE 2021 Primary 5 Mathematics syllabus. It is also needed for mental calculation and estimation in the PSLE.

items.e: × 10: every digit moves 1 place to the left, so write 1 zero at the end. 47 × 10 = 470. (57 adds 10; it does not multiply.)
× 100: every digit moves 2 places to the left, so write 2 zeros at the end. 63 × 100 = 6300.
× 1000: every digit moves 3 places to the left, so write 3 zeros at the end. 8 × 1000 = 8000.
× 10: every digit moves 1 place to the left, so write 1 zero at the end. 250 × 10 = 2500. (25 000 has 2 extra zeros: that is × 100.)
× 100: every digit moves 2 places to the left, so write 2 zeros at the end. 406 × 100 = 40 600. (Keep the 0 in the tens place of 406.)

items.q: Which calculation does the place value chart show?
items.e: Every digit moved 3 places to the left, so it is × 1000. 58 × 1000 = 58 000.
× 10: every digit moves 1 place to the left, so write 1 zero at the end. 3120 × 10 = 31 200.
72 000 is 72 with 3 zeros at the end: every digit moved 3 places to the left. So it is × 1000.
× 1000: every digit moves 3 places to the left, so write 3 zeros at the end. 905 × 1000 = 905 000. (95 000 drops the 0 in the tens place of 905.)
× 100: every digit moves 2 places to the left, so write 2 zeros at the end. 1600 × 100 = 160 000.
Use the inverse: 48 000 ÷ 100. Take away the last 2 zeros: 480. Check: 480 × 100 = 48 000.

items.q: Which calculation does the place value chart show?
items.e: Every digit moved 2 places to the left, so it is × 100. 2370 × 100 = 237 000.
× 1000: every digit moves 3 places to the left, so write 3 zeros at the end. 4050 × 1000 = 4 050 000. (Keep the 0 in the hundreds place of 4050.)

items.q: The chart shows 3684 × 100 = 368 400. What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: Every digit moved 2 places to the left, so the 6 is now in the ten thousands place. Its value is 60 000.
× 10: every digit moves 1 place to the left, so write 1 zero at the end. 7009 × 10 = 70 090. (Keep both zeros inside 7009.)
Use the inverse: 6 400 000 ÷ 1000. Take away the last 3 zeros: 6400. Check: 6400 × 1000 = 6 400 000.

items.q: Which number is 1000 times as large as 520?
items.e: 1000 times as large means × 1000. Write 3 zeros at the end: 520 × 1000 = 520 000. (1520 adds 1000.)

items.q: Which calculation has the answer 30 000?
Hui Min says 2500 × 100 = 25 000. What is her mistake?
c: She wrote 1 zero, not 2; it is 250 000
items.e: × 100 means 2 more zeros at the end. 2500 already has 2 zeros; it needs 2 more: 2500 × 100 = 250 000. 25 000 is only 2500 × 10.
÷ 10: every digit moves 1 place to the right, so take away the last zero. 4800 ÷ 10 = 480. (48 takes away 2 zeros: that is ÷ 100.)
÷ 100: every digit moves 2 places to the right, so take away the last 2 zeros. 36 000 ÷ 100 = 360.
÷ 1000: every digit moves 3 places to the right, so take away the last 3 zeros. 9000 ÷ 1000 = 9. (8000 takes away 1000; it does not divide.)
÷ 100: every digit moves 2 places to the right, so take away the last 2 zeros. 70 500 ÷ 100 = 705. (Only the last 2 zeros go. The 0 in 705 stays: it holds a place.)
÷ 1000: every digit moves 3 places to the right, so take away the last 3 zeros. 250 000 ÷ 1000 = 250.

items.q: Which calculation does the place value chart show?
items.e: Every digit moved 2 places to the right, so it is ÷ 100. 64 000 ÷ 100 = 640.
÷ 10: every digit moves 1 place to the right, so take away the last zero. 3060 ÷ 10 = 306. (The 0 in the hundreds place of 3060 stays.)
÷ 1000: every digit moves 3 places to the right, so take away the last 3 zeros. 5 200 000 ÷ 1000 = 5200.
÷ 100: every digit moves 2 places to the right, so take away the last 2 zeros. 810 000 ÷ 100 = 8100.
Use the inverse: 47 × 100. Write 2 zeros at the end: 4700. Check: 4700 ÷ 100 = 47.
92 000 became 92: the last 3 zeros were taken away, so every digit moved 3 places to the right. It is ÷ 1000.

items.q: The chart shows 1 380 000 ÷ 100 = 13 800. What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: Every digit moved 2 places to the right, so the 3 is now in the thousands place. Its value is 3000.
÷ 1000: every digit moves 3 places to the right, so take away the last 3 zeros. 600 000 ÷ 1000 = 600.
÷ 10: every digit moves 1 place to the right, so take away the last zero. 40 040 ÷ 10 = 4004. (Take away the 0 at the end, not the 0 in the middle.)

items.q: Which calculation does the place value chart show?
items.e: Every digit moved 3 places to the right, so it is ÷ 1000. 8 050 000 ÷ 1000 = 8050.
Use the inverse: 305 × 1000. Write 3 zeros at the end: 305 000. Check: 305 000 ÷ 1000 = 305.
7200 became 720: only the last zero was taken away, so every digit moved 1 place to the right. It is ÷ 10.

items.q: How many hundreds are there in 45 000?
items.e: The number of hundreds is 45 000 ÷ 100. Take away the last 2 zeros: 450 hundreds. Check: 450 × 100 = 45 000.

items.q: Zhi Hao says 60 300 ÷ 100 = 63. What is his mistake?
c: He took away the wrong 0; it is 603
items.e: ÷ 100 takes away the last 2 zeros of 60 300. The 0 in the middle stays: 60 300 ÷ 100 = 603.

items.q: Which calculation has the answer 25?

sets.title: Multiply and divide by multiples of 10, 100 and 1000

items.e: 20 = 2 × 10, so divide by 10 first, then by 2. 2400 ÷ 10 = 240, and 240 ÷ 2 = 120. (24 divides by 10 and then by 10 again, but 20 = 10 × 2, not 10 × 10.)
300 = 3 × 100, so divide by 100 first, then by 3. 3600 ÷ 100 = 36, and 36 ÷ 3 = 12. (1200 forgets the ÷ 100; 36 forgets the ÷ 3.)

items.q: The diagram shows how to work out 35 × 40. What number goes in the last box?

items.e: 80 = 8 × 10, so divide by 10 first, then by 8. 7200 ÷ 10 = 720, and 720 ÷ 8 = 90. (900 forgets the ÷ 10; 720 forgets the ÷ 8.)
400 = 4 × 100, so divide by 100 first, then by 4. 9600 ÷ 100 = 96, and 96 ÷ 4 = 24. (2400 forgets the ÷ 100.)

items.q: The diagram shows how to work out 4500 ÷ 50. What number goes in the last box?
items.e: 50 = 10 × 5, so divide by 10, then by 5. 4500 ÷ 10 = 450, and 450 ÷ 5 = 90. (45 divides by 10 and then by 10 again.)

items.q: Which is the same as 500 × 60?
Priya says 700 × 20 = 1400. What is her mistake?
c: She left out a zero; it is 14 000

items.q: Estimate the value of 38 × 52 by rounding each number to the nearest ten.
items.e: 38 ≈ 40 and 52 ≈ 50. 40 × 50 = 2000. (4 × 5 = 20, then write 2 zeros.) (1500 rounds 38 down to 30, but 38 is nearer to 40.)

items.q: Estimate the value of 69 × 21 by rounding each number to the nearest ten.
Estimate the value of 618 ÷ 19 by rounding 618 to the nearest hundred and 19 to the nearest ten.
items.e: 618 ≈ 600 and 19 ≈ 20. 20 = 2 × 10, so divide by 10 first, then by 2. 600 ÷ 10 = 60, and 60 ÷ 2 = 30. (60 divides by 10, not by 20.)

items.q: Estimate the value of 412 × 29 by rounding 412 to the nearest hundred and 29 to the nearest ten.
Which is the best estimate for 79 × 32?
items.e: Round each number to the nearest ten: 79 ≈ 80 and 32 ≈ 30. So 80 × 30 = 2400. The exact answer, 2528, is close to 2400.

items.q: Estimate the value of 2385 ÷ 61 by rounding 2385 to the nearest hundred and 61 to the nearest ten.
items.e: 2385 ≈ 2400 and 61 ≈ 60. 60 = 6 × 10, so divide by 10 first, then by 6. 2400 ÷ 10 = 240, and 240 ÷ 6 = 40. (240 divides by 10 only.)

items.q: Estimate the value of 587 × 42 by rounding 587 to the nearest hundred and 42 to the nearest ten.
Estimate the value of 47 × 615 by rounding 47 to the nearest ten and 615 to the nearest hundred.
Estimate the value of 1210 ÷ 39 by rounding 1210 to the nearest hundred and 39 to the nearest ten.
Estimate the value of 296 × 403 by rounding each number to the nearest hundred.
Which is the best estimate for 4830 ÷ 59?
items.e: Round 4830 to the nearest hundred (4800) and 59 to the nearest ten (60). 4800 ÷ 60 = 480 ÷ 6 = 80.

items.q: Estimate the value of 704 × 58 by rounding 704 to the nearest hundred and 58 to the nearest ten.
Estimate the value of 8940 ÷ 31 by rounding 8940 to the nearest thousand and 31 to the nearest ten.
Estimate the value of 3106 × 48 by rounding 3106 to the nearest thousand and 48 to the nearest ten.
Estimate the value of 19 × 3980 by rounding 19 to the nearest ten and 3980 to the nearest thousand.
Estimate the value of 35 840 ÷ 589 by rounding 35 840 to the nearest thousand and 589 to the nearest hundred.
Jun Jie works out 52 × 39 = 2028. Which estimate shows that his answer is reasonable?
items.e: Round to the nearest ten: 52 ≈ 50 and 39 ≈ 40. 5 × 4 = 20, then write 2 zeros: 50 × 40 = 2000. 2028 is close to 2000, so it is reasonable.

items.q: Estimate the value of 812 × 49 by rounding 812 to the nearest hundred and 49 to the nearest ten.
Estimate the value of 9870 ÷ 52 by rounding 9870 to the nearest thousand and 52 to the nearest ten.
Ali works out 61 × 48 and gets 29 280. Estimate to check. Which is correct?
c: About 300, so it is not reasonable
About 3000, so it is not reasonable
items.e: 61 ≈ 60 and 48 ≈ 50. 60 × 50 = 3000. 29 280 is about 10 times too big, so Ali’s answer is not reasonable. (The exact answer is 2928.)

items.q: 20 buses take the P5 pupils to Gardens by the Bay. Each bus carries 45 pupils. How many pupils are there?
items.e: 20 units = 20 × 45. 45 × 2 = 90, and 90 × 10 = 900. There are 900 pupils. (90 forgets the × 10.)

items.q: Exercise books come in packs of 100. A school needs 3600 exercise books. How many packs does it need?
items.e: 3600 ÷ 100: take away the last 2 zeros. The school needs 36 packs. Check: 36 × 100 = 3600.

items.q: The school prints 1000 copies of its magazine. Each copy has 36 pages. How many pages are printed?
items.e: 36 × 1000: write 3 zeros at the end. 36 000 pages are printed.

items.q: The school buys 40 chairs for the library. Each chair costs $30. How much do the chairs cost altogether?
items.e: 40 × $30 = 4 × 3 × 100 = 12 × 100. The chairs cost $1200. ($70 adds instead of multiplying.)

items.q: There are 1200 pupils in a school. Each class has 40 pupils. How many classes are there?
During Chinese New Year, Mdm Wong gives 30 red packets. She puts $20 in each red packet. How much money does she give altogether?
items.e: 30 × $20 = 3 × 2 × 100 = $600. Count the zeros: 1 in 30 and 1 in 20 make 2.

items.q: A drinks stall orders 300 cartons of drinks. Each carton has 24 packets. How many packets are there?
The school hall has 50 rows of chairs for Speech Day. There are 40 chairs in each row. How many chairs are there?
Raju’s family saves $300 every month. How much do they save in 20 months?
A lorry carries 6000 kg of rice in bags of 50 kg. How many bags of rice are there?
A library puts 8400 books on 70 shelves. Each shelf has the same number of books. How many books are on each shelf?
A bakery makes 2500 kaya buns a day. How many kaya buns does it make in 30 days?
A printer prints 60 pages in 1 minute. How many minutes does it take to print 4800 pages?
items.e: 4800 ÷ 60: divide by 10, then by 6. 4800 ÷ 10 = 480, and 480 ÷ 6 = 80 minutes.

items.q: A stationery shop has 6000 erasers. It packs them in packets of 20. How many packets does it make?
items.e: 20 = 10 × 2, so divide by 10, then by 2. 6000 ÷ 10 = 600, and 600 ÷ 2 = 300 packets. (60 divides by 10 and then by 10 again.)

items.q: Box A has 100 times as many beads as Box B. Box B has 85 beads. How many beads are in Box A?
items.e: 1 unit = 85, so 100 units = 85 × 100 = 8500. Box A has 8500 beads. (185 adds 100.)

items.q: Farah’s school collects 4200 cans for recycling in 30 days. It collects the same number of cans each day. How many cans does it collect each day?
Ethan runs 20 rounds of a 400 m track during Sports Day practice. How many metres does he run?
19 buses take pupils to East Coast Park. Each bus carries 41 pupils. About how many pupils go? Round each number to the nearest ten.
items.e: 19 ≈ 20 and 41 ≈ 40. 20 × 40 = 2 × 4 × 100 = 800. About 800 pupils go. (The exact number is 779.)

items.q: A school buys 20 boxes of markers. Each box has 30 markers. The markers are shared equally among 40 classes. How many markers does each class get?
items.e: Step 1: 20 × 30 = 600 markers. Step 2: 40 units = 600, so 1 unit = 600 ÷ 40. 600 ÷ 10 = 60, and 60 ÷ 4 = 15. (600 is the total, not one share.)

items.q: Mrs Lim buys 30 tickets for a school concert. Each ticket costs $12. She pays with $400. How much change does she get?
items.e: Step 1: 30 × $12 = 12 × 3 × 10 = $360. Step 2: $400 − $360 = $40. ($360 is the cost, not the change. $364 uses 12 × 3 = 36 and forgets the × 10.)
